entries.lexeme: חרס `khéres` «pottery, earthenware; clay, ceramics» [Kaikki Hebrew، السطر 6163]
entries.route_as_recorded: عزل مسار الاقتراض المنشور قبل المقارنة؛ لا يحول التطابق الصوتي أو الدلالي القرض إلى أثر نسب.
entries.oldest_form_as_recorded: From Hittite 𒂁 (ḫarši-, “a kind of rough pottery vessel”); in the Tanakhic passages it does not mean the material itself, but only a kind of vessel, which apparently derives from Asia Minor with the borrowing. Other Semitic languages have instead of this word a phono-semantic matching, under which are Classical Syriac ܚܶܙܦܳܐ (ḥezəp̄ā), Classical Syriac ܚܶܨܦܳܐ (ḥeṣəp̄ā, “piece of pottery”), whence Arabic خَزَف (ḵazaf), and Ge'ez ጻሕብ (ṣaḥb), ጻኅብ (ṣaḫb, “earthen vessel”).؛ الشاهد القديم: Tanach, Job [[s:he:T2709#ט_ז|9:7]], with translation of the New Revised Standard Version Updated Edition:؛ Tanach, Deuteronomy [[s:he:T0528#כח_כז|28:27]], with translation of the New Revised Standard Version Updated Edition:

entries.oldest_form_as_recorded: Derived from Akkadian 𒆠𒉈 (/⁠kuru⁠/, “crucible, kiln, brazier; log, thick reed; short reed mat, collection of reeds”), likely coined from Sumerian 𒄥 (gur, “a bundle”), hence a place of burning bundles of firewood or tinder.
